name: Conveyor grasping (xArm + 5-finger hand)
summary: A five-fingered hand on an xArm (in the physics, with collisions) learns to see objects dropped on a moving conveyor, reach, grasp with real contact forces and place them in a bin; training can be spr
help: Modes. Learn to see: the camera beside the robot (96x72, depth and colour) feeds a small convolutional network that learns which pixels are the object, where it is, how big and which way it lies (18 training objects, checked on 12 kept for the test). Learn to reach / grasp / place: PPO over thousands of cells (MuJoCo Warp on an NVIDIA GPU, or MuJoCo on the CPU). The xArm 6 is simulated: six position servos with torque limits follow the hand target through inverse kinematics, and the arm, the hand and the fingers collide with the pedestal, the belt frame, the bin and its stand. Objects are dropped onto the moving belt so where they land varies. Each stage carries on from the one before. Parallel tasks (workers): more than 1 runs the round as that many tasks, each on its own worker (any hardware), all starting from the policy given as input; a combine task then averages their policies (weighted by the steps each gathered) into one, written as the round's output: chain rounds for distributed training. Test with new objects: the policy runs live; pick the object, its pose, its turn and the belt speed in the 3D view; the object falls from Drop height onto the moving belt. Make the 3D models: writes the xArm-with-hand and objects robot files for the project's assets; a conveyor .glb wired to Conveyor model is fitted to the belt and baked in. Telemetry channels: joints, scene, events, camera_picture, train (train_1.. for the other tasks), rounds, test.
